summary: This document describes the code of conduct for participants in the Internet Research Task Force. The IRTF holds that research works best in an open and inclusive forum that welcomes diverse ideas and participation, and the code sets expectations for behavior toward that end.

eli5.summary: A club has rules so everyone feels welcome and can share ideas. This is the rulebook for how people should behave in a group of Internet researchers.

subtitle: How to treat people fairly in an Internet research organization

tldr.problem: The Internet Research Task Force (IRTF) is a community of researchers from around the world. As the organization grows and becomes more diverse, it needs clear expectations for how people should treat each other and conduct their work.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC establishes a code of conduct covering harassment and respect, research integrity (proper citation, no plagiarism, transparent AI use), research ethics (approval for human subjects research), inclusive language, and accessibility (remote participation, travel support, fair membership policies).
tldr.outcome: The IRTF is committed to creating an open and inclusive research environment where people from all backgrounds feel welcome and can contribute their best work.

today: RFC 9775 is an informational RFC that was developed by the Internet Research Steering Group (IRSG) with broad consultation from the IRTF community. It represents the IRTF's consensus on conduct expectations and remains the authoritative code of conduct for IRTF participants.

sections.title: Why the IRTF Has a Code of Conduct
sections.content:
The Internet Research Task Force (IRTF) is a community of researchers exploring long-term Internet challenges. Unlike the IETF, which develops standards for near-term needs, the IRTF focuses on speculative research without requiring immediate deployment.

This code of conduct reflects the IRTF's belief that research works best in an open, inclusive forum. The IRTF is not the IETF; it has a different mission and organizational structure, so its code of conduct emphasizes research values over standards-making consensus.

The code covers five areas: respectful conduct and harassment prevention, research integrity, research ethics, inclusive language and imagery, and participation and accessibility. The goal is an environment where all researchers feel respected and can do their best work.
sections.eli5: Scientists researching the Internet meet in groups. They want everyone to feel safe, be honest, respect people from different countries and backgrounds, and let anyone join even if they work from home.

sections.title: Respectful Conduct and Research Integrity
sections.content:
Harassment is behavior that is unwelcome, hostile, or intimidating, including speech that targets people based on education, race, gender, religion, age, disability, sexual orientation, or gender identity. Examples include offensive language, sexual imagery, deliberate intimidation, stalking, unwanted sexual attention, and inappropriate physical contact. The IRTF applies the same anti-harassment policy as the IETF.

Participants who observe or experience harassment can report it to their research group chair, the IRTF Chair, or the Ombudsteam, which works confidentially. The IRTF takes reports seriously and can exclude offenders from activities.

On mailing lists and online forums, moderators prevent harassment and disruption (inflammatory posts, repeated off-topic messages). Moderators can warn, temporarily suspend, or permanently suspend posting rights. Appeals can be made to the IRTF Chair.

Research Integrity requires honesty, transparency, and fairness. Participants must give credit to others, provide evidence for claims, and not engage in plagiarism or misrepresentation of authorship. Falsifying content is prohibited and can result in retraction or exclusion.

Generative AI tools cannot be listed as authors. Using AI to write content is allowed but must be disclosed if significant; using AI for spelling, grammar, or translation need not be disclosed.
sections.eli5: Treat everyone with respect. No mean words or unwanted behavior. Give credit to people whose work you use. Do not copy work without saying so. If you use an AI to write, say which one.

sections.title: Research Ethics and Inclusive Communication
sections.content:
Research involving human subjects or personal data must be conducted ethically and with approval from the researcher's institution (an Institutional Review Board or Research Ethics Committee). The IRTF points participants to established guidance: the Menlo Report and Belmont Report for general ethical principles, and the ACM policy for specifics about human subjects research.

Researchers must consider risks and benefits carefully and ensure that those bearing the risk also gain some benefit. They must respect the law and public interest.

Inclusive Language and Imagery means using words and visuals that are respectful to people from diverse backgrounds. Effective research uses terminology that is clear, precise, and widely accessible. Participants should avoid unnecessary jargon and slang, and make a sincere effort to understand each other if communication difficulties arise.

English is the de facto language of the IRTF, but many participants are not native speakers. All participants, especially native speakers, should accommodate others by communicating clearly and treating non-native speakers with grace and understanding.
sections.eli5: If you study people, get permission from experts. Use clear words that people from other countries understand. If someone speaks English slowly, be patient and kind.

sections.title: Participation and Accessibility
sections.content:
To encourage broad participation, the IRTF expects organizers to consider accessibility when planning meetings and events. Presentations should be clear and slow, and materials should be accessible to people with visual or hearing impairment. Remote participation should be enabled so people who cannot travel can join.

The IRTF provides travel grants, fee waivers, childcare support, and other assistance to help students, early-career researchers, under-represented groups, people with disabilities, and others who might not be able to participate otherwise. Participants are encouraged to use these opportunities.

IRTF research groups can have open or limited membership. Limited membership may help with long-term collaboration but must be used carefully to avoid fragmenting the research community. Group charters define the membership policy, and chairs must enforce it fairly and transparently, providing clear reasons for decisions. Appeals can be made to the IRTF Chair.

In exceptional cases, the IRTF Chair (in consultation with the Internet Architecture Board) may restrict an individual from using IRTF systems or attending events, following legal advice.
sections.eli5: Everyone should be able to join meetings even if they are far away, blind, deaf, or short on money. The group should explain who can join and fairly enforce the rule.
